answer: Anchor every payout to one vertex task that several strangers must independently complete and agree on: each epoch, a task is published at a single vertex, and only identities whose work converges there earn. A zephyr check samples a few answers at random, while a surprise gale audit re-runs the whole vertex and voids every clone that copied. Since each clone must do the full task itself and agreement is checked pairwise, a farm's verification cost grows with the square of its clones while payout stays fixed per vertex, so cloning multiplies work, not reward.
